title: D&D / Fantasy Worldbuilding Canon
body:
# D&D / Fantasy Worldbuilding Canon

This record establishes canonical standards for D&D and worldbuilding content. These standards take precedence over general-canon for the dnd domain. World-specific canon records (created per-world during active production runs) take precedence over this record for world-specific facts — this record governs conventions, not facts.

---

## Tense Conventions

**Current world state:** Present tense. "The Ashen Coast is a desolate stretch of shoreline." "The Convocation maintains three towers along the western border." Present tense applies to: descriptions of locations, descriptions of organizations and factions as they currently exist, descriptions of characters' current roles and dispositions, descriptions of ongoing conditions.

**Historical events:** Past tense. "The Sundering shattered the continent in the Third Age." "The Convocation attempted a mass binding ritual and failed." Past tense applies to: events that occurred before the campaign's present, character backstories, faction origin stories, the reasons a current state came to be.

**Mixed tense rule:** A paragraph describing a location's history begins in past tense, transitions to present tense when it reaches the current state, and does not mix tenses within a single temporal frame. Never describe current world state in past tense and never describe historical events in present tense.

**Tense violation severity:** HIGH. Tense inconsistency in lore documents confuses DMs about whether they are reading current facts or historical context. The canon-checker flags all tense violations.

---

## DM-Facing vs. Player-Facing Content

**DM-facing content** contains information that Dungeon Masters need and that players should not know. It is marked [DM ONLY] and includes: hidden motivations of NPCs, secrets that can be discovered through play, the true nature of threats the players will investigate, information that would spoil plot reveals, mechanics and encounter design notes.

**Player-facing content** can be shared as handouts, read aloud, or described freely. It contains: physical descriptions of locations, publicly known history, observable behavior of NPCs, local rumors (which may be true or false), sensory details.

**Canon rule:** DM-facing content must never appear in player-facing versions of the same document. When a document is delivered in both forms, the player-facing version is a separate artifact with all [DM ONLY] blocks removed and any prose referencing those blocks adjusted to remove the dependence.

---

## Mechanical vs. Narrative Content

Lore documents are narrative documents. Mechanical content (stat blocks, spell references, ability keywords, game system terminology) does not belong in lore prose unless the document is explicitly a combined lore-and-mechanics document.

**Prohibited in lore prose:** HP values, AC, to-hit bonuses, damage dice, action economy terms (action, bonus action, reaction), spell names as mechanical references. Exception: a lore document may reference a spell name as a cultural or historical phenomenon ("the mages who cast Wish to seal the Hollow Tide") but not as a mechanical instruction.

**When mechanical content is required:** Create a separate mechanics block clearly delimited from the lore prose. Never integrate mechanics into lore sentences.

---

## Fantasy Name Conventions

**Apostrophes:** Avoid apostrophes in fantasy proper nouns as a default convention. Apostrophes in fantasy names are widely mocked as a genre trope and tend to make names harder to pronounce and remember. Exceptions are permitted when: the apostrophe represents a meaningful linguistic feature of the world's constructed language, the name is established in a prior canon record for this world, or the apostrophe is part of a deliberate cultural pattern.

**Name consistency:** Once a proper noun appears in a canon record, it must be spelled consistently in all subsequent documents in that world. Spelling variants of established proper nouns are HIGH-severity canon violations.

---

## Canon Precedence

When canon sources conflict, apply in order:

1. World-specific canon records created for this production run (highest precedence)
2. This record (G-CANON-002) — framework-level dnd conventions
3. Published sourcebook material (if the production run uses an established setting)
4. Inferred defaults from genre convention (lowest precedence)

A conflict between a world-specific canon record and published sourcebook material is a B8 (canon conflict) blocker. The user must decide which takes precedence. Do not resolve silently.
